The Weizmann Institute of Science (or simply Weizmann; Hebrew: מכון ויצמן למדע Machon Weizmann LeMada) is a postgraduate university and research institute in Rehovot, Israel.
Type: Public research
Unlike other Israeli universities, it exclusively offers postgraduate-only degrees in the natural and exact sciences.

value.text:
The Weizmann Institute of Science (מכון ויצמן למדע) is a postgraduate university and research institute in Rehovot, Israel. It is described as a public research institution offering postgraduate degrees in the natural and exact sciences. Its multidisciplinary programmes and research activities distinguish its graduate-only educational focus from universities that also admit undergraduates.

Chaim Weizmann and his initial team established the Daniel Sieff Research Institute in 1934. On 2 November 1949, following agreement with the Sieff family, it adopted the Weizmann Institute of Science name. Scientists at the institute built the early electronic computer WEIZAC in 1954–1955. In 1959, it established the wholly owned Yeda Research and Development Company to commercialize inventions arising from institute work. These events describe institutional development rather than a merger with another university.

Graduate programmes include M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees in mathematics, computer science, physics, chemistry, biochemistry and biology, together with interdisciplinary programmes. An institutional infobox reports 1,700 students in 2025 and separately lists postgraduate and doctoral counts without explaining whether the categories overlap. The campus in Rehovot includes research buildings and residential facilities; a campus description records its land area as 1,250 dunams. The reported enrolment and physical scale are tied to particular sources and should not be treated as live totals.
